{"id":"PKIX-i39n","title":"pkix-revocation reports PKITS 4.15.5 Valid delta-CRL Test5 as revoked","description":"PKITS 4.15.5 'Valid delta-CRL Test5' expects the chain to VALIDATE. pkix-path reports:

  pkix-path revocation: cert at chain index 0 revoked by CRL: certificate 04 is revoked (reason c...)

pyca agrees ('pyca: certificate 0x4 revoked by CRL'). OpenSSL passes.

PKITS §4.15.5 exercises a certificate placed on hold by the base CRL and then released by the delta CRL. RFC 5280 §5.3.1 gives removeFromCRL (8) for exactly that: an entry in a delta CRL with that reason means the certificate is no longer revoked and must be removed from the local CRL cache. If a delta is applied without honouring removeFromCRL, a released certificate stays revoked -- which is what the reported reason (certificateHold) suggests happened.

That direction is FAIL-CLOSED: a usable certificate is refused, not a revoked one accepted. Lower urgency than the reverse, but still wrong, and it means delta-CRL support is incomplete rather than merely strict.

pyca failing the same way is not evidence pkix-path is right -- it is evidence both share the gap, with OpenSSL and NIST on the other side.

To verify: check whether pkix-revocation's delta-CRL application handles CrlReason::RemoveFromCrl at all, and whether the base entry is dropped when a delta carries it.

One of two remaining real ground-truth disagreements after PKIX-vcpy removed the 13 caused by unapplied policy inputs.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-26T02:37:21.384568146Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-26T02:37:21.384568146Z"}
